grh_7e7c73d0f2e2934d12e1.title: Action -Joseph Kearns
paragraphs: After a mild stroke convinces Christopher Bell that he will soon become helpless, the aging mountaineer chooses an impossible glacier climb as a disguised suicide. Near exhaustion he hears a woman in danger and saves her; she claims she too sought death because of an incurable illness, and they make a pact to keep living. The closing revelation is that her doctor husband and actress wife deliberately staged the encounter to give Bell a reason to live.

grh_7e66c0b91793ad5a11dd.title: Hyacinth Patrol
paragraphs: During a stop near the Panama Canal, Harry befriends American sergeant Tiger Dolan and becomes entangled in suspicions about an officer secretly meeting an enemy contact. With help from Rita, a local girl, Harry confirms that an espionage ring is using a hidden communications post to coordinate an attack intended to cripple the canal and its dam. The agents capture Harry and Dolan and prepare to kill them while signaling an offshore carrier and its bombers. Rita has already gone for help, however, and Dolan's Hyacinth Patrol arrives in time to storm the hideout. The spy network is rounded up, the attack is stopped and the enemy carrier is destroyed before the canal can be bombed.

This [[show|the-lives-of-harry-lime|The Lives of Harry Lime]] broadcast aired on February 29, 1952. It is listed as episode 31 in the archive. The cast includes [[person|orson-welles|Orson Welles]] and Anton Karas. Other credited names include Tig Roe as director and Harry Alan Towers as producer.

grh_7ee3110f7deeabb04fec.title: The Group
paragraphs: After an elderly woman in an apartment building is beaten to death, police suspect that the killer may be one of the emotionally disturbed patients in a psychiatrist's therapy group. During a tense group session, suspicion first focuses on one member, but the doctor uses the patients' reactions and a psychological reconstruction of the murder to expose Stephen as the real killer. Stephen pulls a gun and threatens the doctor, who keeps talking to the frightened, abused child beneath the violence until Stephen breaks down and surrenders the weapon. The doctor insists that the task is to destroy the murderous behavior while still trying to save the human being behind it.

grh_7e1f8c1a64691e923231.title: Full Employment in a Free Society
paragraphs: A policy dramatization of William Beveridge's Full Employment in a Free Society frames the postwar economy as a fork in the road between Depression and Full Employment. A returning veteran is shown the human cost of mass unemployment, then guided through Beveridge's argument that government should sustain demand, protect citizens from unemployment and support social security, health care, education and decent housing. Critics challenge the plan as excessive state control, while the broadcast answers that full employment is meant to remove fear and insecurity without abolishing individual freedom.

This [[show|words-at-war|Words at War]] broadcast aired on April 3, 1945. [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Jack Arthur, Martin Wolfson, Humphrey Davis, Harold Young, and Abby Lewis. Other credited names include Anton M. Leader as director and Ben Kagan as radio adaptor.
The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes.
This version dramatizes [[work|work.words.704654c3629565a0|Full Employment in a Free Society]]. William Beveridge is credited as author and Ben Kagan adapted it for radio.
